answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a reputation bond — call it nectar — that accrues only through verified useful work over weeks, not account creation. An attacker spinning up thousands of clones hits a basalt wall: every clone must independently earn its bond before transacting, so cost scales linearly with fake identities while reward stays flat. Honest agents cluster in a trusted oasis of mutual attestation, where established peers vouch for newcomers and lose their own bond if the newcomer cheats.
